summary: Checked all 18 round-1 findings and the four additional round-2 findings against the revised documents. ATLAS-008 and ATLAS-014 remain incompletely resolved. Two new defects affect held-candidate approvals and sandbox filesystem access. The remaining earlier findings are resolved at the documented architecture level.

findings.description: Queued and armed merges now have a state, but still lack a cancellation policy when ATLAS authorization expires or is revoked. Once GitHub holds the merge request, it can merge without another G-MERGE-PRE evaluation.
findings.evidence: MERGE_PENDING_REMOTE polls and reacts to remote cancellation, dequeueing or head changes. Neither its transitions nor reconciliation cancel the remote request after approval expiry, a policy-version change, or disabling auto_merge. G-MERGED checks identity and reachability, not authorization. Disabling queue support by default limits exposure but does not make the documented enabled path safe.
findings.recommendation: Define authorization semantics for pending remote merges and an outbox operation to cancel queued/armed requests when authorization becomes invalid. Reconcile cancellation before allowing repairs or replacement delivery intents. Keep support unavailable until these paths are implemented and tested.

findings.description: Review and handoff execution references still enforce only project ownership, allowing evidence to be associated with an execution for a different candidate within the same project.
findings.evidence: review_rounds independently references candidate_id and execution_id through project-scoped foreign keys. A review of candidate A can therefore reference an execution of candidate B. handoffs constrains candidate-to-phase but likewise references its execution only by project. The enumerated relationship validators cover test executions and handoff candidate-to-phase consistency; the additional transactional validation addresses NULL components, so it does not close these fully populated mismatches.
findings.recommendation: Enforce review/handoff execution-to-subject consistency through composite foreign keys or explicit transactional validators, including plan-review executions. Add negative tests with fully populated references to different candidates and phases in the same project.

findings.description: A held candidate can pass all diff guards using an approval for only one category of violation.
findings.evidence: guard_status records only clear or held. G-DIFF accepts an approved protected_path/destructive_migration/secret_change approval for the candidate and policy version, without requiring its kind to match every failed guard. A candidate containing both a protected workflow edit and a destructive migration therefore passes with only a protected_path approval.
findings.recommendation: Persist the complete set of failed guards and require a current, matching approval for every violation before TESTING and delivery. Apply the same check to the AWAITING_APPROVAL exit.

findings.description: The sandbox filesystem requirements simultaneously allow verification worktrees and explicitly deny their enclosing ATLAS directory, leaving the default test execution boundary contradictory.
findings.evidence: The profile permits reads and writes to the verification worktree but explicitly denies ~/.atlas with an exception only for the execution's own sandbox directory. The documented worktrees and project clones live beneath ~/.atlas/worktrees and ~/.atlas/projects. Verification worktrees are not specified to live inside the exempt sandbox directory. A profile enforcing the blanket denial cannot execute tests against those worktrees; weakening that denial broadly exposes ATLAS state.
findings.recommendation: Specify verification worktrees under the per-execution sandbox directory, or define narrow worktree exceptions with explicit rule precedence while keeping the database, artifacts, credentials and other worktrees inaccessible. Extend the self-test to prove both candidate access and state isolation.
